_comment: The half of the LCA parameters that is not an openLCA emission factor: values that
differ per vehicle model or per charging point type. lca.json holds the rest.
Shaped like tco.json, not like the file of the same name in eflips-x. That one is a
list keyed by VehicleType.name_short, and eflips-impact's init_lca_params() writes
nothing at all -- for any entity -- if a single battery-electric vehicle type in the
scenario is missing from it. django-simba fleets come from user uploads and have
arbitrary names, so a name-keyed list would match nothing and silently leave the
whole scenario unparameterised. 'vehicle_type_default' therefore covers every
battery-electric vehicle type, and the diesel block every diesel one.
'year' selects the electricity mix from lca.json's per-year series, which drives
the entire use-phase impact of a battery-electric fleet. It is a fixed constant
rather than something derived from the scenario, because django-simba stores no
project year anywhere. Values between the years in lca.json (2023, 2030, 2050) are
interpolated; values outside that range are clamped, with a warning.
'motor_rated_power_kw' is applied to every vehicle type equally. Motor mass is
derived from it as power / power_to_weight_ratio, so an articulated bus is given
the same motor as a 12 m one, understating its production emissions. Correcting
this needs a per-type figure, most likely a rule based on VehicleType.length.
Consumption is deliberately absent. eflips-impact reads it from these parameters,
but ebustoolbox.impact writes it in from the simulated driving events after the
run, the same value the TCO calculation uses. A number here would only be a
second, unused source for it.
